seo.title: Washington, D.C. Homeless Help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified shelter, food, health, employment, benefits, legal aid, and other help for people experiencing homelessness in Washington, D.C.

page.heading: WASHINGTON, D.C. - HOMELESS HELP
page.urgent: Immediate danger or medical emergency: 911 Shelter, outreach, and free transport to shelter: 202-399-7093 or 311 Mental health or substance use crisis: call or text 988, or call 888-793-4357 Crime or domestic violence support: call or text 844-443-5732
page.notice: Information can change. Call ahead when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, appointment, meal, service, job, benefit, or approval. Shelter is first come, first served unless a program says otherwise. If you have nowhere to sleep tonight, start with Emergency shelters.
page.footer: No Home Help is a lightweight, open-source directory. It is not an emergency service and does not operate the organizations listed.

entries.title: DC Shelter Hotline and street outreach
entries.description:
If you need a place tonight, call the Shelter Hotline first. DC low-barrier shelters accept people on a first-come, first-served basis. The hotline can check current options and arrange free, accessible transport. It cannot promise that a bed will still be available when you arrive.
Phone: 202-399-7093 or 311
Hotline hours: daily, 8 a.m. to midnight; 24 hours from November 1 through March 31.
Help: shelter information, wellness checks, outreach, blankets or water when available, and free accessible transport to shelter or a warming site. Outreach normally operates Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., with longer hours during cold-weather activations.
- Call the Shelter Hotline — tel:+12023997093
- Official shelter information
- Official outreach information — https://dhs.dc.gov/page/outreach-0

Adams Place: 2210 Adams Place NE

Official low-barrier shelter guidance

entries.title: Virginia Williams Family Resource Center - families

Family shelter placements are made through intake; family shelter buildings are not walk-in sites. Call before going and bring household documents if you have them. After hours, call the Shelter Hotline.
Official family shelter information

entries.title: Youth emergency shelter

Official DC youth shelter list

Phone: 202-745-7118
Official help information

entries.title: Cold-weather and extreme-weather help
entries.description:
From November 1 through March 31, the Shelter Hotline operates 24 hours. Additional hypothermia sites open as the system approaches capacity. During an Extreme Cold Alert, open sites may extend to 24-hour operation.
Do not wait for symptoms of hypothermia. Call 202-399-7093 or 311 for transport.
Current cold-weather information

entries.title: Coordinated Assessment and Housing Placement
entries.description:
DC uses a decentralized, no-wrong-door coordinated-entry system. A trained provider can assess housing needs and connect eligible people to available programs. An assessment is not a housing offer and does not guarantee placement.
Where to start: a day center, shelter, street-outreach team, Miriam's Kitchen, Friendship Place, SOME, or another participating provider.
Official coordinated-entry information

entries.title: Friendship Place Welcome Center
entries.description:
Phone: 202-364-1419

Official drop-in and clinic information
entries.address: Address: 4713 Wisconsin Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20016

entries.title: Preventing homelessness
entries.description:
If you still have housing but face eviction, unpaid rent, or unsafe conditions, contact Legal Aid DC or the Washington Legal Clinic promptly. Emergency rental assistance and prevention programs often have funding limits, appointments, and documentation rules; apply before a court date or move-out when possible.
- Legal Aid DC
- Washington Legal Clinic for the Homeless — https://www.legalclinic.org/get-legal-help/

categories.title: Medical, mental health, and recovery care

entries.title: Unity Health Care for people experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Call 911 for a medical emergency. Call or text 988 for a mental health, substance use, or suicide crisis. The services below are not emergency departments.
Main phone: 202-508-0500
Primary care, case management, and other health services at shelters and day centers. Unity accepts patients regardless of ability to pay; free or discounted fees may be available based on income. Walk-in sites include Downtown Day Services Center, Federal City/CCNV, Central Union Mission, Friendship Place, New York Avenue Shelter, N Street Village, and Pathways to Housing. Clinic schedules differ, so call first.
Official homeless health program

entries.title: Unity at Downtown Day Services Center
entries.description:
Phone: 202-508-0500
Typical clinic hours: Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to noon. Walk-in. Confirm before traveling.
Official Unity locations
entries.address: Address: 1313 New York Avenue NW, basement suite 1

entries.title: Unity at Federal City/CCNV
entries.description:
Phone: 202-508-0500
Typical hours: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Walk-in. This is one of Unity's most comprehensive homeless health sites.
Official Unity locations
entries.address: Address: 425 2nd Street NW, Washington, DC 20001

entries.title: Bread for the City medical clinic
entries.description:
New-patient phone: 202-386-7020
Primary care for adults and children, examinations, medications, labs, referrals, harm reduction, and coordinated behavioral, dental, and vision care. Care is provided regardless of ability to pay; dental and behavioral programs generally serve established primary-care patients.
Official clinic information and call times

entries.title: SOME medical and dental clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 202-797-8806
Official services
entries.address: Address: 60 O Street NW, Washington, DC 20001
entries.hours: Hours: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; walk-in registration is normally 8 to 11 a.m. Serves adult DC residents and also connects people to mental health and recovery services.

entries.title: DBH Access Helpline
entries.description:
Phone: 888-793-4357, TTY 711
Official helpline information
entries.hours: Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week. Crisis support, referral to ongoing mental health or substance use care, and activation of mobile crisis teams for people unable or unwilling to travel.

entries.title: Community Response Team - crisis response on the street
entries.description:
Phone: 202-673-6495
Official team information
entries.hours: Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week. On-the-spot assessment, short-term support, referral, harm-reduction options, and outreach by clinicians and peers.

entries.title: DC Stabilization Center - substance use crisis
entries.description:
Eligibility and cost: free and voluntary for adults 18 or older; no insurance or DC residency required. Services include medical screening and stabilization, peer support, food, clothing, showers, laundry, and connection to longer-term treatment.
Official center information
entries.address: Address: 35 K Street NE, Washington, DC 20002
entries.hours: Hours: 24 hours a day, every day; walk-ins welcome.

entries.title: Assessment and Referral Center - treatment enrollment
entries.description:
Phone: 202-727-8473
Official access information
entries.address: Address: 75 P Street NE, Washington, DC
entries.hours: Hours: Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Call for an appointment or walk in for assessment and referral to detoxification, outpatient, residential, medication-assisted, and recovery services.

entries.title: Whitman-Walker Health
entries.description:
Affirming primary care, HIV and sexual health care, behavioral health, insurance navigation, and legal services, with particular expertise serving LGBTQ+ people and people living with HIV.
Official health services and locations

entries.title: DC day centers
entries.description:
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, and 801 East provide toilets during open hours. They also offer indoor space and other survival services. Ask staff before leaving belongings unattended.
Official locations and hours

entries.title: DC Public Library
entries.description:
DC Public Library has 26 locations. The central Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library is at 901 G Street NW. Libraries provide indoor public space, toilets during open hours, computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning. Rules and holiday hours apply.
Find the nearest open library

entries.title: Day-center computers and charging
entries.description:
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, and 801 East list phone charging and computer access. Availability may be limited; bring your own cable and stay with your device.
Official day-center list

entries.title: Free library computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning
entries.description:
All DC Public Library locations offer public computers and Wi-Fi. Computer use is first come, first served. The library currently offers up to 20 pages a day of free printing, copying, or scanning.
- Computer and printing rules
- Library locations — https://www.dclibrary.org/plan-visit

entries.title: Digital Navigators
entries.description:
Library Digital Navigators provide one-to-one help with phones, computers, email, online forms, PDFs, printing, and online privacy at selected branches. Drop-in availability varies; call the branch first.
Current Digital Navigator locations

entries.title: Free transport to shelter or warming sites
entries.description:
Call the DC Shelter Hotline at 202-399-7093 or 311. The hotline can arrange free, accessible transport to an available shelter or extreme-weather site. Transport does not reserve a bed.
Official transport information

entries.title: Metro Lift - 50% discount for SNAP recipients
entries.description:
People currently receiving SNAP in DC, Maryland, or Virginia can apply for 50% off Metrobus and Metrorail fares. Enrollment requires an active EBT card, a SmarTrip card, current government photo identification, and a phone number.
In-person enrollment: Transit Accessibility Center, 655 Virginia Avenue SW, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Walk-ins are welcome.
Official eligibility and enrollment

entries.title: Senior and disability reduced fares
entries.description:
Metro offers 50% reduced fares for riders age 65 or older and for riders under 65 with qualifying disabilities. The disability program requires an application and Reduced Fare Photo ID.
- Official fare programs
- Transit Accessibility Center — https://www.wmata.com/ride/accessibility/transit-accessibility.html

entries.title: Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA)
entries.description:
Airports are not shelters. If you are stranded without a safe place to sleep, call the Shelter Hotline before leaving a staffed public area. Metro service does not run all night.
The airport has its own Metrorail station on the Blue and Yellow lines. Use the WMATA trip planner for current service, elevator status, and fare. Metro Lift discounts apply to eligible cards.
WMATA trip planner

entries.title: Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD)
entries.description:
The Silver Line serves Dulles Airport. The station connects to the terminal through an indoor pedestrian walkway of roughly five minutes. Train hours and final departures differ by day; check before traveling late at night.
- Official Dulles Silver Line guide
- WMATA trip planner — https://www.wmata.com/schedules/trip-planner/

entries.title: District Direct - SNAP, Medicaid, and cash assistance
entries.description:
Phone: 202-727-5355, TTY 711
Call-center hours: Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
Apply online through District Direct, by paper application, fax, mail, or at a DHS Service Center. Programs include SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, and other cash or medical assistance. Applying does not guarantee eligibility.
- District Direct — https://districtdirect.dc.gov/
- Official application instructions

entries.title: DHS Service Centers - in-person benefits help
entries.description:
Locations: Anacostia, Fort Davis, Congress Heights, H Street, and Taylor Street. Any center can help; DC uses a no-wrong-door policy. Check the official page for same-day closures before traveling.
Current addresses and operating status
entries.hours: Hours: Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., except holidays.

entries.title: Benefits help without navigating alone
entries.description:
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, 801 East, Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center, SOME, and Bread for the City can help people understand or apply for benefits. Ask for a benefits navigator or case manager; assistance and eligibility vary.
Start with a DC day center

entries.title: DC American Job Centers
entries.description:
Phone: 202-724-7000
Career counseling, resumes, job search and placement, training, labor-market information, and unemployment assistance. Current in-person services may require an appointment.
- Official job-seeker services
- Locations and appointments — https://does.dc.gov/service/american-job-center

entries.title: DCNetworks
entries.description:
DCNetworks is the District's job-search system. You can search openings, post a resume, and apply online. Library computers and Digital Navigators can help if you do not have a device.
Search jobs on DCNetworks

entries.title: SOME Center for Employment Training
entries.description:
Phone: 202-797-8806
Occupational training and employment support. Programs have intake requirements and scheduled start dates; call before going.
Official SOME help directory
entries.address: Address: 4430 Benning Road NE, Washington, DC

entries.title: Job search at day and youth centers
entries.description:
Downtown Day Services Center and Adams Place offer employment assistance and computers. Sasha Bruce provides job search and readiness help for young people. N Street Village connects women to training and employment opportunities.
- DC day centers
- Sasha Bruce — https://www.sashabruce.org/drop-in-center/
- N Street Village — https://www.nstreetvillage.org/housing-community/

entries.title: Washington Legal Clinic for the Homeless
entries.description:
Phone: 202-328-5500
Free legal help with shelter denials, street rights, housing programs, public benefits, identification, discrimination, record sealing, and other civil issues affecting people experiencing homelessness. If you are denied safe, accessible shelter, call this number.
Official intake information
entries.address: Address: 1200 U Street NW, Washington, DC 20009
entries.hours: Hours: Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

entries.title: Legal Aid DC
entries.description:
Phone: 202-628-1161
Northwest: 1331 H Street NW, Suite 350; walk-in Tuesday and Thursday, 12:30 to 4 p.m.
Southeast: 1911 Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue SE; walk-in Monday and Thursday, 12:30 to 4 p.m.
Free civil legal services for eligible low-income DC residents. Capacity and case acceptance vary.
Official contact and intake information

entries.title: DC Bar Advice and Referral Clinic
entries.description:
Free Saturday civil legal advice from volunteer attorneys; no appointment. Intake is normally 10 a.m. to noon and capacity is limited. The clinic operates on selected dates, not every Saturday.
Check upcoming clinic dates
entries.address: Address: 901 4th Street NW, Washington, DC 20001

entries.title: Whitman-Walker free legal services
entries.description:
Phone: 202-939-7630
Help with health insurance and public-benefit appeals, disability, discrimination, immigration, medical privacy, and name or gender-marker changes. An intake is required; acceptance is not guaranteed. Interpretation, including ASL, is available.
Official legal services

entries.title: Ayuda - immigrants
entries.description:
Ayuda provides legal, social, and language services for low-income immigrants in DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Contact the organization for current intake availability; do not pay an unverified person for immigration advice.
Official Ayuda website

entries.title: No-fee DC birth certificate and non-driver ID
entries.description:
Eligible DC residents experiencing homelessness may obtain a no-fee DC birth certificate or non-driver identification card through a DHS-designated access point. A provider must verify eligibility and participation in homeless services; this is not a walk-in fee waiver at every government office.
Current access points include: Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, 801 East, Community Connections, Zoe's Doors, Shirley's Place, Latin American Youth Center, SAMU, and Sasha Bruce.
Important: current DC rules require recent HMIS history and documented service engagements. Ask an access-point worker to check eligibility before going to Vital Records or DMV.
Official requirements and access-point list

entries.title: Downtown Day Services Center document help
entries.description:
Staff can help with vital records and DMV identification vouchers. DMV services are scheduled on site on certain days. Call 202-383-8810 before going specifically for documents.
Official center information
entries.address: Address: 1313 New York Avenue NW

entries.title: Youth document help
entries.description:
Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center helps young people obtain identification and vital records. Zoe's Doors and Latin American Youth Center are also designated ID access points.
- Sasha Bruce services
- DC youth centers — https://dhs.dc.gov/page/youth-homeless-services

entries.title: SOME mail service
entries.description:

Official mail-service information
entries.address: Service location: 61 O Street NW, Washington, DC 20001
entries.hours: Hours: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.

entries.title: Youth mail service
entries.description:
Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center at 741 8th Street SE lists mailing services for young people experiencing homelessness or housing instability. Register with staff before using the address.
Official services

entries.title: Adams Place Day Center - limited storage

Washington has very limited public storage for people experiencing homelessness. Do not assume that a shelter will store belongings or accept large bags.
The official day-center flyer lists limited storage. Space, duration, and item rules can change. Ask staff in person or call 202-374-6846; availability is not guaranteed.
Official Adams Place flyer
entries.address: Address: 2210 Adams Place NE

Confidential crisis support and connection to emergency safety, shelter, legal, financial, medical, and emotional resources for victims of crime. If making a call could put you in danger, use a safe device or ask a trusted service provider to help.
Official hotline information
entries.hours: Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week.

Official Ayuda website

Phone: 877-424-3838
Official national hotline
entries.hours: Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week. Free and confidential for veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk, and for family members or supporters calling on their behalf.

entries.title: Department of Aging and Community Living
entries.description:
The Information and Referral unit helps older adults, adults with disabilities, and caregivers find social services, health programs, public benefits, long-term supports, and other assistance.
Official information and referral service

entries.title: Disability access and accommodation
entries.description:
Tell the Shelter Hotline or a shelter worker if you need an accessible vehicle, mobility accommodation, sign-language access, a service-animal accommodation, or another disability-related change. If safe, describe the specific barrier and keep a record of requests.
If you are denied safe, accessible shelter, call the Washington Legal Clinic for the Homeless at 202-328-5500.
DC disability-service information

entries.title: Humane Rescue Alliance Pet Help Center
entries.description:
Ask the Shelter Hotline about current pet and service-animal rules before traveling. A service animal is not the same as a pet; explain any disability-related accommodation you need.
Free pet food and supplies at partner locations, affordable veterinary-care information, behavior support, and crisis resources intended to help people keep their animals. Programs and stock change, so contact the center before traveling.
Official Pet Help Center

entries.title: DC Animal Care and Control
entries.description:
Phone: 202-888-7387
Lost or found animals, animal emergencies, and information about the current DC animal shelter operator. Call rather than leaving an animal unattended at a facility.
Official animal-control information

entries.title: If you do not know where to start
entries.description:
1. Call 202-399-7093 or 311 if you need shelter or street outreach.
2. Go to the nearest open day center for toilets, hygiene, charging, case management, and multiple services in one place. — #hygiene
3. Ask for a coordinated housing assessment, benefits screening, and document help.
4. Write down the name, date, and next step after every referral. Return or call again if a program tells you to check back.
